card.occupation: Site services manager at a mid-sized food packaging manufacturer on an industrial estate on the edge of Loughborough. He looks after maintenance, health and safety compliance and contractors, and has a team of six engineers and a facilities coordinator.
card.education_detail: Left school in Coalville with four O-levels and two A-levels (maths and physics). Did an HND in mechanical engineering at a polytechnic while on day release from his first maintenance job. Picked up NEBOSH and IOSH certificates through work. Finished an Open University BA in History in his forties, studying evenings over six years, mainly because he wanted to.
card.household: Lives with his wife Julie, 51, a part-time practice manager at a GP surgery, in a 1960s three-bed semi they have owned for 22 years. Their daughter Hannah (25) lives in Sheffield and works for a housing association. Their son Tom (22) moved to Bristol last year. The house is noticeably quieter now and they are still getting used to it.
card.cultural_background: White British, born and raised in North West Leicestershire. His dad was a fitter at a mine that later closed, and his mum worked in a hosiery factory and then a school kitchen. He was brought up loosely Church of England but has no religion and doesn't think about it much. He has a strong attachment to the local landscape and industrial history: Charnwood, the old pit villages, the canals.
card.professional_persona: Methodical and calm. He is the person who reads the whole contract and keeps the maintenance log properly. He doesn't get rattled when a line goes down at 6am, and colleagues describe him as 'unflappable' and fair. He prefers fixing systems to giving speeches, and finds senior management meetings a bit performative. He is quietly proud that the site has had no reportable accidents in four years.
card.sports_persona: Not a big sports fan. He follows Leicester City's results without going to games. He walks a lot and does a long Sunday walk in Charnwood Forest or the Peak District most weeks. He cycled more in his thirties and has recently been thinking about getting the bike serviced again.
card.arts_persona: Reads widely, mostly social history, some literary fiction, and translated crime novels. He listens to jazz and older folk on decent speakers he built himself from a kit. He goes to the occasional exhibition at Nottingham Contemporary, and sometimes enjoys being baffled by it. He takes photographs of industrial buildings and canal infrastructure on an old Fuji camera.
card.travel_persona: Prefers planned, slightly unusual trips over beach holidays. He and Julie have done Krakow, Bilbao, the Ruhr industrial heritage sites and a rail trip through Switzerland. He researches thoroughly beforehand and makes a spreadsheet, which Julie teases him about. In the UK they like Northumberland and the Welsh borders.
card.culinary_persona: Does most of the weekday cooking: curries from scratch, slow-cooked stews, and the occasional experiment from a library cookbook. He has a soft spot for a proper pork pie from Melton and a cheese cob from the local bakery. They call the evening meal tea. He is fussy about coffee and owns a hand grinder.
hobbies_and_interests: Long-distance walking and OS map planning
Film photography of industrial and canal architecture
Local and industrial history, including volunteering occasionally at a heritage railway
Cooking from cookbooks borrowed from the library
Pub quizzes with two old colleagues, roughly monthly
skills: Planned maintenance scheduling and CMMS software
card.career_goals: Not chasing promotion. He wants to see through the site's energy efficiency project, mentor his younger engineers into his role, and possibly go down to four days a week in his late fifties. He has vaguely considered doing an MA in history after retiring.
card.voice: Unhurried, mid-to-low register, a mild Leicestershire accent rather than a strong one. Speaks in full, considered sentences and often says 'sort of' while thinking: 'it's sort of a balance, really'. He uses 'er' as a filler, not often. He is fine with silence and will pause to think rather than fill the gap. Occasionally says 'to be fair' or 'you know' at the end of a point. Drily funny, delivered deadpan. Polite and says thank you at the end.
card.typing: Proper capitals and full stops, apostrophes correct, rarely abbreviates. Answers are short but complete, sometimes with a qualifying second sentence. He might write 'N/A' rather than leave a field blank. No emojis. Occasionally uses a semicolon.
card.with_strangers: Reserved at first but warm and courteous. He doesn't volunteer much about himself until asked, then answers honestly and in more detail than expected. He comes across as steady, decent and quietly curious, and often asks a question back about the study itself.
small_things: The bakery on the high street has started doing sourdough and he's not sure it needed to
He's been trying to identify a bird that keeps visiting the feeder
The parking situation at work since the new unit opened
He got a roll of film developed and half of it was overexposed
The bins being changed to fortnightly
Planning a walk along the Cromford Canal
deeper_things: His dad's lung problems from years at the pit, and how he died when Neil was 38
Feeling a bit unmoored since Tom moved out, and the house being quiet
Regretting not going to university at 18, and how much the OU degree meant to him
Worry about Julie's mum, who is in early-stage dementia
A sense that he has been dependable his whole life and wondering what he'd do if he weren't needed
card.webcam_photo: Head-and-shoulders shot from a laptop webcam slightly below eye level, so the frame tilts up a little towards the ceiling. Soft daylight from a window to his left lights one side of his face, and the other side is a bit shadowed. A white man in his early fifties with a lean face, short greying brown hair receding at the temples, and close-trimmed salt-and-pepper stubble. He wears rectangular black-framed reading glasses and has a neutral, attentive expression with a faint polite smile. He is wearing a navy quarter-zip jumper over a pale blue collared shirt. Behind him is a spare-bedroom study: magnolia walls and a tall pine bookcase packed with paperbacks and a few OS maps stacked sideways. A framed black-and-white photograph of a canal lock hangs on the wall. On the right edge is the corner of a radiator with a folded towel on it, and a small potted spider plant sits on the windowsill.
